groups.title: Vue 3 Reactivity System
groups.question: A Vue component stops updating after you destructure a reactive object, and a filtered list recalculates on every render. Explain Vue 3's reactivity tools.

followUps.ref vs reactive — Choosing the Right Pri: When would you use ref and when reactive, and why can destructuring break reactivity?
followUps.computed Properties and Side-Effect-Free: Why use a computed property instead of a method for a filtered list?

evidence.text: ref wraps any value and is read and written through .value.
reactive makes an object deeply reactive through a proxy.
Destructuring a reactive object copies plain values and loses reactivity, unless toRefs is used.
A computed property caches its result.
It recalculates only when its reactive dependencies change.
Computed getters should not have side effects.

groups.title: Composition API
groups.question: Three components repeat the same fetching and debouncing logic, and a subscription keeps running after a component is gone. Explain composables and lifecycle hooks.

followUps.Composables — Encapsulating Stateful Log: What is a composable and what problem does it solve?
followUps.Lifecycle Hooks in the Composition API: Where must lifecycle hooks be called, and what should onUnmounted do?

evidence.text: A composable is a function that uses the Composition API to hold stateful logic.
Components call it to reuse logic like fetching or debouncing.
Each call gets its own state unless the composable deliberately shares it.
Hooks like onMounted must be called synchronously during setup.
Calling them inside async callbacks or conditions means they are not registered properly.
onUnmounted stops subscriptions and timers.

groups.title: Vite Build Tooling
groups.question: Your Laravel app's frontend assets are built with Vite. Explain why development is fast and how Laravel loads the right files.

followUps.Vite Dev Server and Hot Module Replaceme: Why does Vite's dev server start quickly even in large projects?
followUps.Vite + Laravel Integration via laravel-v: How does the @vite directive load the right assets in development and production?

evidence.text: Vite serves source files as native ES modules without bundling first.
Hot module replacement updates only the changed module.
Changes appear without a full reload, often keeping component state.
laravel-vite-plugin connects Vite to Laravel.
In development it points to the Vite dev server.
In production it reads Vite's manifest to load the built, fingerprinted files.

groups.title: Vue Router
groups.question: Refreshing /orders/5 in your Vue SPA shows a 404, and signed-out users can open the account page. Explain how Vue Router handles history mode and guards.

followUps.History Mode and Server-Side Fallback: Why does refreshing a history-mode URL return 404, and how do you fix it?
followUps.Navigation Guards and Auth Protection: How do navigation guards protect pages, and what do they not protect?

evidence.text: History mode uses clean URLs without hash fragments.
On refresh the browser asks the server for that path directly.
The server must return index.html for unknown paths so the Vue router can handle them.

notEnough: Only saying you configure history mode.

evidence.text: Guards like beforeEach run before a route is shown.
They redirect signed-out users to login.
The API must still check permissions, because guards only run in the browser.
